Food table

There have been tons of changes to the food table in the game. You will notice that most of the mushrooms are kept under the name "Amanita" and the orange mushrooms are under the name "Chanterelle". Herbs and berries replaced mushrooms and some recipes requiring mushrooms were removed (in correspondence to update @v.618).

Notice that a camp with a dugout will double food durability and that some buildings increase it, even more, the highest being the Moroz's Terem.

Bread grants the bonus :

  • Hearty food. The bonus lasts 2 days and its effects (per hour) are
    • +1
    • +2


Nutrition Score

Each consumable item can be given a “nutrition score” based on the fact that water declines twice as fast as food, and 1 energy gained by sleeping “consumes” 1 Food and 1 Water. This gives us a value ratio of 1/2/3 for Food, Water and Energy respectively. Note that health, radiation and additional effects are not factored into this score.

Food items that can be obtained by crafting/cooking often use consumable ingredients, and have an additional “cooking score” shown in parentheses which subtracts the nutrition score of consumable ingredients which are safe-to-eat, as well as the cooked version of unsafe ingredients which are safe to eat cooked. This shows how crafting the item affects the nutrition of your items.

Example:

Mushroom Soup provides +35 and +15, giving it a base Nutrition score of 35+(15x2) = 65. However, in order to make it, you have to use a Chanterelle and 3 Clean Water. The Clean Water has a Nutrition Score on its own of (25x2)x3 = 150, and while the Chanterelle is not safe to eat raw, it can be cooked, which gives it a Nutrition Score of 15x1 = 15. Together, this comes out to a total ingredient Nutrition Score of 165. We can subtract this from the Nutrition Score of the Mushroom Soup to give it a “cooking score” of 65-165 = -100, representing a steep loss in nutritional value.

On the chart below, Mushroom Soup is therefore listed as having a Nutrition Score of 65(-100).

Despite this, Mushroom Soup grants the very powerful buff of Training I, which means the player should weigh the lost food and water against the value of this effect when deciding to craft it.
